```{r}
#Libraries
library(sf)
library(terra)
library(tidyverse)
```

```{r}
#Check the layers of the raster data to decide which to use for the task
#Also you can use QGIS to show what the layer is representing
st_layers("data/gadm41_SAU.gpkg")

# HOW TO DECIDE:
#   - "features" = number of polygons in that layer.
#   - Level 0 has 1 feature = the whole country. That's what we need
#     to crop/mask the rasters to the national boundary.
#   - Level 1 would be useful if you wanted stats per province.

```

```{r}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. COUNTRY OUTLINE (GADM)  -- checking which LAYER to read

 
saudi <- st_read("data/gadm41_SAU.gpkg", layer = "ADM_ADM_0")
 
# Quick checks on what you loaded:
saudi            # prints attributes + geometry type + CRS


st_crs(saudi)    # coordinate reference system (should be WGS 84 / EPSG:4326)


plot(st_geometry(saudi))   # visual check: does it look like Saudi Arabia?
 
# NOTE: if you leave out layer = ..., st_read() reads the FIRST layer
# and warns you that others exist.
```
```{r}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. WORLD CITIES (Esri shapefile)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# A shapefile only has ONE layer, but you can still check:
st_layers("data/World_Cities.shp")
 
cities <- st_read("data/World_Cities.shp")
 
# Check the column names -- you need to know which column holds the
# country name and which holds the city name before filtering:
names(cities)
head(cities)
 
# Check how Saudi Arabia is spelt in the data (avoid typos in filter):
unique(cities$CNTRY_NAME) %>% sort()

```


```{r}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. WORLDCLIM RASTERS -- checking the LAYERS (bands)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
ssp1 <- rast("data/wc2.1_2.5m_tmax_ACCESS-CM2_ssp126_2081-2100.tif")
ssp5 <- rast("data/wc2.1_2.5m_tmax_ACCESS-CM2_ssp585_2081-2100.tif")
 
# Rasters also have "layers" (called bands). Check them:
ssp1             # summary: dimensions, resolution, extent, CRS, nlyr
nlyr(ssp1)       # number of layers -> should be 12 (one per month)
names(ssp1)      # default layer names (long, taken from the file)
 
# Rename the 12 layers to month names.
# names() <- is base R and works on rasters.
# (dplyr::rename() only works on data frames / tables, NOT rasters.)
month <- c("Jan","Feb","Mar","Apr","May","Jun",
           "Jul","Aug","Sep","Oct","Nov","Dec")
names(ssp1) <- month
names(ssp5) <- month
 
names(ssp1)      # check it worked
 
# Look at a single layer, e.g. July:
plot(ssp1[["Jul"]])
```

```{r}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. FILTER CITIES TO SAUDI ARABIA + MATCH CRS
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
saudi_cities <- cities %>%
  filter(CNTRY_NAME == "Saudi Arabia") %>%
  st_transform(crs(ssp1))          # make CRS match the raster
 
nrow(saudi_cities)                 # how many cities did we get?
saudi_cities$CITY_NAME             # which ones?
 
# Optional check: do CRS match?
st_crs(saudi_cities) == st_crs(saudi)
```


```{r}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. CROP & MASK RASTERS TO SAUDI ARABIA
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# crop() = cut to the bounding box (rectangle) of the country
# mask() = set cells OUTSIDE the country outline to NA
ssp1_sa <- ssp1 %>% crop(saudi) %>% mask(saudi)
ssp5_sa <- ssp5 %>% crop(saudi) %>% mask(saudi)
 
plot(ssp5_sa[["Jul"]])
plot(st_geometry(saudi_cities), add = TRUE, pch = 19)
```

```{r}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. DIFFERENCE RASTER (SSP5 - SSP1)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Because both rasters have the same 12 layers in the same order,
# subtraction is done month-by-month (Jan - Jan, Feb - Feb, ...)
diff <- ssp5_sa - ssp1_sa
names(diff)      # still Jan..Dec
plot(diff)
```

```{r}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. EXTRACT VALUES AT EACH CITY
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
city_diff <- terra::extract(diff, vect(saudi_cities)) %>%
  mutate(city = saudi_cities$CITY_NAME[ID])
 
city_diff        # one row per city, one column per month
 
# CHECK FOR NAs: coastal cities (e.g. Jeddah, Dammam) may fall just
# outside the masked outline.
city_diff %>% filter(is.na(Jan))
 
# FIX if needed: extract from the CROPPED but UNMASKED rasters instead
# diff <- crop(ssp5, saudi) - crop(ssp1, saudi)
# then re-run step 7.
```

```{r}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. RESHAPE TO LONG FORMAT
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Wide: city | Jan | Feb | ... | Dec
# Long: city | month | diff      <- easier for stats and ggplot
long <- city_diff %>%
  pivot_longer(Jan:Dec, names_to = "month", values_to = "diff") %>%
  mutate(month = factor(month, levels = month.abb))  # keep Jan-Dec order
```

```{r}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# 9. DESCRIPTIVE STATISTICS
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Per city
city_stats <- long %>%
  group_by(city) %>%
  summarise(mean = mean(diff, na.rm = TRUE),
            min  = min(diff,  na.rm = TRUE),
            max  = max(diff,  na.rm = TRUE),
            sd   = sd(diff,   na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(desc(mean))
city_stats
 
# Per month (across all cities)
month_stats <- long %>%
  group_by(month) %>%
  summarise(mean = mean(diff, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd   = sd(diff,   na.rm = TRUE))
month_stats
 
# Overall
summary(long$diff)
```

```{r}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# 10. PLOTS
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Histogram of all city-month differences
ggplot(long, aes(x = diff)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.25) +
  labs(x = "Tmax difference SSP5 - SSP1 (°C)", y = "Count",
       title = "Saudi Arabian cities, 2081-2100 (ACCESS-CM2)")
 
# Boxplot by month -- is the gap bigger in summer?
ggplot(long, aes(x = month, y = diff)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(x = "Month", y = "Tmax difference (°C)")
 
# Boxplot by city -- which cities warm most?
ggplot(long, aes(x = reorder(city, diff), y = diff)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = "City", y = "Tmax difference (°C)")
```

```{r}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# 11. MAP (optional, but helps interpret the statistics)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Quick look with base terra:
plot(diff[["Jul"]], main = "July tmax difference SSP5 - SSP1 (°C)")
plot(st_geometry(saudi), add = TRUE)
plot(st_geometry(saudi_cities), add = TRUE, pch = 19)
 
# Nicer map with ggplot2.
# Step 1: average the 12 monthly bands into ONE band (annual mean diff)
diff_annual <- mean(diff)          # cell-by-cell mean across the 12 layers
names(diff_annual) <- "diff"
 
# Step 2: ggplot can't plot a SpatRaster directly, so convert to a
# data frame with x, y coordinates + the value of each cell
diff_df <- as.data.frame(diff_annual, xy = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE)
head(diff_df)                      # columns: x | y | diff
 
# Step 3: build the map in layers
ggplot() +
  geom_raster(data = diff_df, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = diff)) +   # raster
  geom_sf(data = saudi, fill = NA, colour = "black") +            # outline
  geom_sf(data = saudi_cities, size = 1.5) +                      # city points
  geom_sf_text(data = saudi_cities, aes(label = CITY_NAME),       # labels
               size = 3, nudge_y = 0.4) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "inferno",
                       name = "Tmax diff (°C)") +
  labs(title = "Difference in max temperature: SSP5-8.5 minus SSP1-2.6",
       subtitle = "Annual mean, 2081-2100, ACCESS-CM2 (2.5 min)",
       x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
 
# Save it:
# ggsave("saudi_tmax_diff_map.png", width = 8, height = 7, dpi = 300)
```
